items.title: Final Fantasy 7 Director Kept 'Open World Fatigue' in Mind as New Remake Chapter Promises 'Bigger' World Than Rebirth
items.description: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi has acknowledged the "open world fatigue" affecting the industry but says Square Enix was "very careful" to make sure fans would have "all the guidance they need" in the new remake chapter – even if it's bigger than the last.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi has acknowledged the "open world fatigue" affecting the industry but says Square Enix was "very careful" to make sure fans would have "all the guidance they need" in the new remake chapter – even if it's bigger than the last.

The developer helping lead the finale to its 2027 launch spoke about its size during a conversation with Eurogamer. In the interview, he teased how the team has done its best to tie a bow on the trilogy with one final adventure for Cloud, Tifa, Barret, and the rest of the gang in their fight against Sephiroth.

The two previous installments in the remake trilogy – Final Fantasy 7 Remake and Rebirth – have been lumped into online conversations about enormous open worlds that sometimes overstay their welcome. Hamaguchi said the concept of open world fatigue is "very important" to him, but it sounds like players won't need to worry about feeling too lost.

"There are a lot of open world games out in the world right now, and [the idea of 'open world fatigue'] is a very important concept to me," he replied when Eurogamer asked about feedback to Rebirth. "It depends on personal preference and different perceptions, but for me personally, I know I've had the experience where I've been thrown out into an open world game and not known where to go, not known where to begin, and not known what to do. But at the same time, the concept of being thrown into this wondrous world where anything goes is amazing."

There are certainly players who would prefer to get lost in a vibrant fantasy universe. In a world promising to be as packed as Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, that idea might be especially enticing. Hamaguchi said that, as a creator, he believes it's important to "offer proper guidance" in open-world games so that players "know what to do, and know where to go."

"In Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, we made sure to make it easy for the players to understand how much content there is, and how difficult that content is," he added. "That design philosophy is applied to Revelation: players have all the guidance that they need. This is something that both myself and the development team were very careful about when we designed the game."

It seems Hamaguchi and the rest of the development team wanted to strike a balance when it came to guidance in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. One example he mentioned involved asking players to rely on their memory to make sure they land in their desired location when dropping from the Highwind airship.

"That's another example of the guidance we're giving players, without directing them too much," Hamaguchi continued. "The world is even bigger than it was in Rebirth, so it is more important than ever for us to ensure there's enough guidance here, so people have no issues enjoying what this game has to offer."

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation currently has no firm release date but is expected to launch for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X | S in spring 2027. While we wait for updates, you can read about what Hamaguchi had to say about the feedback to Remake and Rebirth's vast pool of mini-games. You can also learn about the leak that suggests DLC may be in development.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Sets Nintendo Switch 2 Release Date for Early August
items.description: Square Enix has announced Final Fantasy 14 has a Nintendo Switch 2 release date of August 4, 2026.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Square Enix has announced Final Fantasy 14 has a Nintendo Switch 2 release date of August 4, 2026.

Game director Naoki Yoshida (a.k.a. Yoshi-P) suited up in Bastion armor and took the stage at Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin to confirm the news alongside a laundry list of new updates coming in the near future. While Square Enix had previously confirmed plans to bring FFXIV to Switch 2 in August, today's news locks in a launch that's only a little more than one week away.

Preorders begin later today, with fans told to keep an eye on Square Enix social media for updates. When FFXIV goes on sale August 4, its first month of sale will be free of subscription charges as the developers ensure server stability. After this period comes to an end, players will be required to purchase a subscription as normal.

"We knew that you've been waiting for this for a long time," Yoshi-P said via translator, "so we're very happy to bring this to you."

Final Fantasy 14 Fan Fest 2026 also allowed Yoshi-P to go back over some of the catches that come with the Switch 2 version of the game. As revealed at Anaheim Fan Fest in April, FFXIV for Nintendo fans will require a separate subscription.

Yoshi-P said at the time that the decision to require an individual subscription on Switch 2 came after "many months of discussions with Nintendo," but it's not all bad news. A Nintendo Switch Online subscription won't be required to play, for example. Additionally, those who have active FFXIV subscriptions elsewhere can take advantage of a 50% discount on Switch 2.

FFXIV is only days away from its Switch 2 launch. Also revealed during the presentation was more information on the upcoming Evercold expansion, the Bastion tank role, a new Final Fantasy 7 collaboration, and more.

For more, you can read IGN's original 8.6/10 review. You can also read about how the game rewards Japanese players for paying their real-life taxes.

items.title: Absolute Batman and Absolute Martian Manhunter Win Big at the 2026 Eisner Awards | Comic Con 2026
items.description: DC's Absolute Universe dominated the 2026 Eisner Awards, with both Absolute Batman and Absolute Martian Manhunter taking home key trophies.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
The winners of the the 2026 Will Eisner Comic Industry Awards were revealed at San Diego Comic-Con. DC took home some major awards on the strength of its Absolute Universe line, with both Absolute Batman and Absolute Martian Manhunter being honored. In total, DC was the most decorated publisher with 10 awards (including Best Continuing Series, Best Limited Series, and Best One-Shot/Single Issue), followed by Image Comics with four awards.

items.title: Spaceballs: The New One Creators on Making Mel Brooks' Yogurt CGI and Paying Tribute to John Candy | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Rick Moranis appeared at SDCC alongside Josh Gad to reveal new details for Spaceballs: The New One, including Mel Brooks' now CGI Yogurt and fresh Star Wars gags.
items.author: Eric Goldman
items.content:
The Schwartz was stronger than ever in Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con. A packed room of thousands of fans cheering on the panel for a sequel nearly 40 years in the making, Spaceballs: The New One.

Rick Moranis' presence was an understandable major deal for the audience, with the comedy legend making his long-awaited return to the screen as he reprises his role as the villain Dark Helmet. Moderator Kevin Smith introduced Moranis with what turned into an elaborate bit where he failed to walk on stage, only for some costumed Spaceball soldiers "combing the crowd" (giant comb included, naturally) to find him. When Moranis actually did take the stage, he got a massive standing ovation.

Not there in person was another legend, original Spaceballs writer and director Mel Brooks, with the 100 year old (!) sending a very funny video, in which he cracked jokes like, “Sorry I can’t be there! I’m on convention floor trying to buy a rare Charizard card!” and "When I was your age, on a Friday, I’d go to something called 'work.'"

Brooks' age came up when discussing him reprising his role as Yogurt. In the original film, Brooks wore elaborate makeup, but Brooks told director Josh Greenbaum and writers Josh Gad (who also produced), Dan Hernandez and Benji Samit that while he was excited to participate, he couldn't do the makeup anymore. Instead, Yogurt will now be a digital character, with Brooks providing the voice. Greenbaum laughed about how Brooks had dots on his face at his first voice recording sessions for the mocap team to use as reference points, only for Brooks to declare "I don’t need the dots.” Greenbaum got the OK from the VFX supervisors to proceed without them.

It was Gad who got the ball rolling on Spaceballs returning inspired to do so after he and Moranis were going to make a Honey, I Shrunk the Kids follow-up that never came to be. He pitched his idea to Brooks, who was excited by it. Gad said he felt the time was right for a Spaceballs sequel because it can comment on how we are living in an age of nostalgia and how there is now so much more Star Wars to parody when the first Spaceballs only had the original trilogy as its basis.

Gad apologized that even though this is a parody of Star Wars, they still were keeping actual secrets like a Star Wars movie, including details on new characters played by Keke Palmer and Gad (though Lewis Pullman is confirmed to play Starburst, the son of Bill Pullman's Lone Star and Daphne Zuniga's Queen Vespa). Gad said he wanted Spaceballs: The New One to be a love letter to someone who sat alongside Moranis on Gad's personal comedy Mount Rushmore, the late John Candy. Gad stressed he was not playing Candy's character, Barf, but is playing another Mawg, Barf's alien species. Gad also promised an that there will be an acknowledgement in the film to other original Spaceballs cast members who have passed away, including Joan Rivers, Dick Van Patten and Dom DeLuise.

The panel ended with a montage of footage from the film that was a slightly re-edited version of the footage first shown at the Amazon AMC CinemaCon panel in April. Some of the gags from that earlier version — such as a Harry Potter parody moment — were removed, but there were also new bits, like Dark Helmet proclaiming "Somehow I've returned... somehow!" We also see a Doctor Strange-style portal open, glimpses of Palmer's character Destiny sporting a decidedly Rey-influenced look, and many other rapid-fire gags, including Yogurt getting hit by a freeze blast and someone proclaiming, "Frozen Yogurt!" It was all backed by a choir singing the Spaceballs theme song from the original film.

The Spaceballs panel was also notable for being one of the rare Hall H panels to use the special side screens, usually saved for would-be epic event movies that want to make a visual impact. This made it all the funnier when the filmmakers did a mock Spaceballs Cinematic Universe slate reveal that included dozens of titles that spanned 11 phases with titles like 2 Space 2 Balls, Pizza the Hutt: Cheesy Does It, Spaceballs vs. Spaceballs vs. Spaceballs, The Space and The Balls, Spaceballs: The Lawsuit, Spaceballs: Enough is Enough, and Spaceballs: Enough is Never Enough.

Moranis said it was the right time for him to return in Spaceballs: The New One, noting he had a terrific time making it. "I was in that outfit and I was in the helmet and it felt really strange and it started to feel really good and I started to love it," he said about being on set again. "And who knows? Maybe it’s the beginning of many." (Just probably not 11 phases worth...)

Gad also promised an that there will be an acknowledgement in the film to other original Spaceballs cast members who have passed away, including Joan Rivers, Dick Van Patten and Dom DeLuise.

The panel ended with a montage of footage from the film that was a slightly re-edited version of the footage first shown at the Amazon AMC CinemaCon panel in April. Some of the gags from that earlier version — such as a Harry Potter parody moment — were removed, but there were also new bits, like Dark Helmet proclaiming "Somehow I've returned... somehow!" We also see a Doctor Strange-style portal open, glimpses of Palmer's character Destiny sporting a decidedly Rey-influenced look, and many other rapid-fire gags, including Yogurt getting hit by a freeze blast and someone proclaiming, "Frozen Yogurt!" It was all backed by a choir singing the Spaceballs theme song from the original film.

The Spaceballs panel was also notable for being one of the rare Hall H panels to use the special side screens, usually saved for would-be epic event movies that want to make a visual impact. This made it all the funnier when the filmmakers did a mock Spaceballs Cinematic Universe slate reveal that included dozens of titles that spanned 11 phases with titles like 2 Space 2 Balls, Pizza the Hutt: Cheesy Does It, Spaceballs vs. Spaceballs vs. Spaceballs, The Space and The Balls, Spaceballs: The Lawsuit, Spaceballs: Enough is Enough, and Spaceballs: Enough is Never Enough.

Moranis said it was the right time for him to return in Spaceballs: The New One, noting he had a terrific time making it. "I was in that outfit and I was in the helmet and it felt really strange and it started to feel really good and I started to love it," he said about being on set again. "And who knows? Maybe it’s the beginning of many." (Just probably not 11 phases worth...)

items.content:

items.title: Next Kratos-Led God of War Game Is Coming After Laufey, and Connects Directly to Her Story | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Santa Monica Studio head of creative Cory Barlog has announced that the next Kratos-led God of War game is coming after God of War Laufey, and connects directly to her story.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Santa Monica Studio head of creative Cory Barlog has announced that the next Kratos-led God of War game is coming after God of War Laufey, and connects directly to her story.

Confirmation comes from the God of War Laufey panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, which IGN reported on live here.

No further details were offered at the panel, although God of War Laufey now has a confirmed release date of February 16, 2027. We have no indication yet when this Kratos-led God of War game will come out, or which platform it is targeting. Nor do we have confirmation of its title or its setting.

During the panel, Barlog said of God of War Laufey that he wanted to see an extension and expansion of the world where the characters we meet are unexpected. "Everything we are doing in the Faye game is a continuation of what came before and to set up and expand what comes next," he explained. "Phranque has been around since the beginning. It's interesting to see how to build this world out. Everything in the game is setting up for something so amazing."

In June, following the reveal of the Faye-starring next chapter of God of War, Santa Monica Studio discussed Kratos' future as the figurehead of its flagship franchise. Speaking in an interview uploaded to PlayStation's YouTube channel, Barlog said that "there's always going to be Kratos games" — a position backed up by a later post from the company's official social media account, which stated that the studio had "many more stories to tell with him."

Early reaction to God of War Laufey has been mixed, with some fans praising the game's combat and visuals, while others have criticized the simplistic gameplay seen in Laufey's opening section — and, predictably, the fact that fan-favorite Kratos wasn't center stage. (For a full catch-up, we’ve got an explainer on Faye herself for more on her story.)

"Faye is, while it's a different thing, it's still part of the larger tapestry of what we truly really want to explore, all of these different characters in there," Barlog said of the new game. "But there's always going to be Kratos games, like, throughout the whole history. We're super excited about that."

"Oh for sure," added Lawrence. "We can't not tell stories about the big guy."

Our first glimpse at God of War Laufey, seen in a 20-minute gameplay segment aired at the end of June's PlayStation State of Play showcase, began with Kratos and Atreus burning Faye's body — as seen in 2018's God of War. Kratos then pops up again shortly after, aiding Faye while she's briefly imprisoned. It remains unclear if Kratos will make any other appearances before Laufey's credits roll, or if these brief glimpses of the hero are it, as he's then busy with the events of God of War Ragnarök.

"Kratos is the God of War – we have many more stories to tell with him," Santa Monica Studio's official X/Twitter account wrote in a post. "For now, we're excited to take fans on a journey into the afterlife of the gods with Faye and hope you’ll come along for the ride!"

Of course, Santa Monica Studio has also announced a remake of the God of War Greek trilogy remake — which will see Kratos back in the spotlight. The original God of War launched back in 2005 for PS2, with its sequel arriving two years later. God of War 3, for PS3, then debuted in 2010. No release date for the God of War Trilogy Remake was announced, and work is still in its "early stages."

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: American Caper From Absurd Ventures' Dan Houser Is Getting a Double-Sized Season Finale Issue #12 - Exclusive | Comic Con 2026
items.description: IGN can exclusively reveal that American Caper, the crime fiction comic series from the mind of Absurd Ventures' Dan Houser, is getting a double-sized season finale issue #12 that will arrive on November 11, 2026.
items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
IGN can exclusively reveal that American Caper, the crime fiction comic series from the mind of Absurd Ventures' Dan Houser, is getting a double-sized season finale issue #12 that will arrive on November 11, 2026.

Houser and producer/contributing writer Lazlow stopped by IGN's live show to share the big news on the "messy season conclusion" that will see the "end of our time in Wyoming." The story is far from over, however, as Houser added that, "we are moving from a red state to a blue state for the next story arc that will begin in a few months after the end of issue 12."

"It’s a crescendo of chaos in the small town of Verona, Wyoming as Marty’s party turns into a family affair crashed by a slew of unwelcome guests," Issue #12's synopsis reads. "Orson admits some not so charming truths to Eliza. Marnie hunts down her husband hellbent on revenge. Eva faces off against the cartel assassin. And Dre BK keeps it calm and brings the namaste mid-firefight through copious amounts of hallucinations and yoga as the Verona chapter of American Caper comes to a very violent conclusion."

The double-sized issue from Absurd Ventures that is being published by Dark Horse Comics will feature 44 story pages, and there will be three covers you can see below;

Cover A by Series Cover Artist Tyler Boss

Variant Cover B by Becky Cloonan

“I've been a huge fan of David Lapham's for as long as I can remember--Stray Bullets was a formative read for me, a masterclass in storytelling and fearless characterization at a time when I was in my early years making comics," Cloonan said. "Smash cut to last year, and he's teamed up with Dan Houser and Lazlow, with Lee Loughridge on colors?? Gimme a break. That is a murderer’s row, and this book is unhinged in the best way possible. Of course I wanted to draw a cover!

"Daniel Chabon is co-editing with Shelly Bond (who I worked with at Vertigo), so when it came time to brainstorm visual themes the team suggested something along the lines of my old Shade the Changing Girl covers. Now, okay, this book is maybe the anthesis to Shade, but it made a lot of sense: the colors, the surreal, almost absurdist vibe... I just leaned into that, and away I went.”

Variant Cover C by Caroline Cash

“I was thrilled when editor Shelly Bond reached out about this series. What a fun ride!! It’s not everyday that you read a story as fresh as this one, and it was a blast to contribute a variant cover for it," Cash said.

“It’s a variant cover to end all variant covers," Bond added. "Who else would get the parallel of a gritty satire like American Caper with The Great Muppet Caper but the current epic cartoonist of Bushmiller’s Nancy strip?”

If you are new to American Caper, which is from the mind of Houser, who was the co-founder of Rockstar Games and longtime head writer and creative director of the Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption series, Absurd Ventures just released the first volume of the series, called Red-Pilled Blues, that gathers the series' first four issues in one collection.

Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

items.title: X-Men '97 Season 3 Will Bring Back These Fan-Favorite Mutant Villains | Comic Con 2026
items.description: X-Men '97 fans just got a big update on Season 3 at Comic-Con, including the return of some fan-favorite mutant villains.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
X-Men '97 fever is burning hot right now, and Marvel fanned the flames at Comic-Con with the "Marvel Comics to Screen" panel. The panelists revealed new details about the upcoming third and fourth seasons, including the return of several fan-favorite mutant villains.

Fans can expect to see the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants to return in Season 3. These characters have been conspicuously absent so far in the revival series, so it's good to know that's going to change soon.

What's more, attendees got an early look at Season 3 in the form of a clip featuring these characters. We see the team -- consisting of Pyro, Avalanche, Blob, and Toad -- in the streets and writing "mutant freedom" on the side of a building. Intriguingly, they're joined by a new recruit in the form of the electricity-wielding teenage mutant Surge, who charges up their graffiti with a massive blast of power. The Brotherhood are then attacked by a new Sentinel variant decked out in patriotic blue colors.

That clip gives us some idea of the tone of the series in Season 3. While the X-Men will presumably win their final battle with Apocalypse this season, it seems tensions with the US government are still running high in the aftermath.

Executive producer Brad Winderbaum also gave attendees a quick update on the status of the next two seasons, revealing that as Season 2 airs right now, they're wrapping up animation work on Season 3 and animatics on Season 4. Hopefully, that means we'll see Season 3 at some point in 2027.

For more on X-Men '97, check out IGN's spoiler-free review of Season 2, Episodes 1-4. And be sure to visit IGN's SDCC hub page for plenty more coverage from the show.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky.

media:description.$text:
4. X-Men '97

One of the most anticipated and widely acclaimed Disney+ series so far was this direct sequel to the beloved 90s X-Men: The Animated Series. While fans were excited to return to that nostalgic world, X-Men '97 became a breakout hit with a weekly release schedule that allowed theories and word of mouth to take hold. Speaking to a wide audience both familiar with the original Saturday morning cartoon and new to the lore, X-Men '97 was a phenomenon in the summer of 2024. It certainly didn't hurt that the show's sophisticated storytelling managed to distill classic X-Men comic book arcs into individual episodes that sped through Chris Claremont's long-gestating plot points without sacrificing meaningful character development.

The devastating impact of X-Men '97's standout episode — the midseason shocker, "Remember It" — combined with Channing Tatum's performance in Deadpool & Wolverine to reinstate Gambit as a core member of the mutant strikeforce. The animators' fondness for the Ragin' Cajun and the voice acting of A.J. LoCascio made the pink-powered playboy a fan favorite again for the first time since the 90s. Season 2 may be at least a year away, but the effects of this brilliant animated series can be felt in the current state of Marvel's publishing line, with Gambit featured in the current Uncanny X-Men series. So hop over to the comics to sate your appetite for more mutant action until the next episodes drop.

items.title: Marvel Comics Makes Eddie Brock Venom Again | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Marvel Comics is bringing Venom back to basics, as Eddie Brock dons the symbiote once more in a new monthly series launching in October 2026.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
Eddie Brock may be separated from the Venom symbiote in Marvel's comic book universe, but don't expect that status quo to last much longer. Today at Comic-Con, Marvel announced that Eddie will become Venom again in a new ongoing series launching after the Queen in Black crossover wraps.

As revealed at Marvel's "Next Big Thing" panel, the new series will be helmed by writer Charles Soule (Star Wars), artist Tommaso Bianchi (Thunderbolts), and cover artist Davide Paratore. You can see art for Venom #1 and the other books featured at the panel in the slideshow gallery below:

Here's the official summary for Venom #1:

Eddie Brock and Venom are reunited — and it feels so good! After years apart, once again THEY ARE VENOM, and Eddie is not going to let this opportunity go to waste. He is determined to be the ultimate host for the symbiote and be the hero he knows he can be…and he’s not going to let any other super heroes say otherwise! Writer Charles Soule (DAREDEVIL, STAR WARS) and artist Tommaso Bianchi (DAREDEVIL/PUNISHER: THE DEVIL’S TRIGGER, THUNDERBOLTS) bond together to bring us this story of two becoming one!

This new series brings Venom full circle. Previously, the symbiote passed from Eddie to his son Dylan and then to Mary Jane Watson. But what of MJ? She'll be starring in a new series of her own, as she embraces a relatively more normal status quo again. Friendly Neighborhood Mary Jane sees MJ resume her Hollywood career, this time as a producer, and butt heads with the Chameleon. The five-issue series is written by Ashley Allen (Tomb of Apocalypse) and drawn by Phil Noto (Daredevil & Echo).

Venom #1 will debut in October 2026, followed by Friendly Neighborhood Mary Jane in November.

Also at the panel, Marvel revealed a new series of crossover specials spinning out of the pages of Phillip Kennedy Johnson's Infernal Hulk series. This lineup includes Infernal Hulk vs. Wolverine #1, Infernal Hulk vs. Fantastic Four #1, Infernal Hulk vs. Spider-Man #1, and Infernal Hulk vs. Avengers #1. All are written by Johnson and help lay the foundation for the upcoming Hulk War event.

IGN’s live reporting of San Diego Comic-Con 2026 continued with the God of War Laufey panel, and there were plenty of announcements!

God of War Laufey game director Ariel Lawrence and Santa Monica Studio head of creative Cory Barlog led an in-depth conversation with the cast, including Deborah Ann Woll (Laufey), Chris Judge (Kratos), Jack Quaid (Phranque), and Perlina Lau (Rue). We got plenty of insight into God of War Laufey itself, but also confirmation that the next Kratos-led God of War game is due out after, and will connect to Faye's story. We also got confirmation of God of War Laufey's release date, which, as expected, is next year. Check out all the details from the panel below.

While you wait for the game to come out, check out IGN’s exclusive coverage of God of War Laufey from its reveal in June. We have Lawrence and Barlog discussing why the developer went with Faye as the main character this time instead of Kratos, and we’ve got an explainer on Faye herself if you need a catch-up on her story.

Friday, July 24 and Saturday, July 25, IGN will stream live from San Diego with A-list interviews, exclusive reveals, and live coverage of SDCC’s biggest panels and announcements. Our broadcast runs from 3pm PT / 6pm ET to 7pm PT / 10pm ET each day and streams across IGN platforms. Here's our live show schedule.

And that's a wrap!

The God of War panel is over. We got some big news here, including confirmation that the next Kratos-led God of War game is due after God of War Laufey, and that God of War Laufeylaunches February 26, 2027. Thanks for being here with us for all the latest!

God of War Laufey release date announced!

We have a release date for God of War Laufey! As expected, it's 2027. Specifically, it's February 16, 2027.

Jack Quaid's cube

Jack Quaid says he felt "at home" in the cube. "All cube related memories were amazing. Most of my time was in a voice over booth," he adds.

Barlog says he wanted to see an extension and expansion of the world where the characters we meet are unexpected. "Everything we are doing in the Faye game is a continuation of what came before and to set up and expand what comes next," he adds. "Phranque has been around since the beginning. It's interesting to see how to build this world out. Everything in the game is setting up for something so amazing."

Quaid says Phranque doesn't know a lot about his past, so he's very present, being in the here and now. "I'm a very anxious person and I'm always thinking about the future, it's nice to play a character in the moment," he says. He's used to playing characters that scream, so he's happy that isn't the case here. He sees hope in Faye. Phranque is very much an innocent, Quaid says, "and there is something where I bring that out of Faye as well."

Who is Faye?

Deborah Ann Woll says she would call Faye 'Faye McClane,' after John McClane from Die Hard. She is a "reluctant hero." "Okay I'll save the day and save the building while I'm at it," she says.

"I always thought that Faye was the genesis of the change of Kratos," Judge adds. "So much of the message in the first two games was about hope and forgiveness and being better. I think that all started with Kratos' relationship with Faye. That's where it began in him and what kept him going was ensuring that this wonderful life that we had created together would be better than the old man."

The cast speaks...

After that bombshell, Deborah Ann Woll (Laufey) says she's pinching herself that she gets to be on this panel at all. She says she hadn't played video games in about 10 years. 2018's God of War had just come out, and she spent all night watching it.

Chris Judge talks about getting the role of Kratos 13 years ago, and how reluctant he was at first. Perlina Lau (Rue) says she received an email from Sony to ask for a chat, and thought it was a scam. "I had a meeting with the casting team and then an audition and a chemsity test with Deborah then I heard nothing," Lau says. "I'll never forget I got in the car one weekend put my phone out saw the email headline. Saw the offer and threw my phone down. I was like omg I can't tell anyone. It's been pretty life changing."

Jack Quaid (Phranque) says he's been a PlayStation fanboy since Crash Bandicoot, and is a huge God of War fan. He "flipped out" when he was offered the role. "I'm on a Zoom with Cory and Ariel and they told me I'm gonna be a cube," he says. "I'm like, 'Okay!" When they say jump I ask how high."

A new God of War game!

Cory Barlog kicked off the panel by announcing another God of War game, starring Kratos, that connects to God of War Laufey! It's due out after Laufey. This is a huge surprise coming out of SDCC!

We're slightly delayed...

We're still waiting for the God of War panel to begin, as people are still being shuffled into Ballroom 20. We'll have more as soon as it happens!

Not long now...

The God of War Laufey panel starts in less than 30 minutes. Check back here for all the news at it happens!

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: 5 Biggest Reveals From the Lanterns San Diego Comic-Con Panel | Comic Con 2026
items.description: The Lanterns panel at San Diego Comic Con revealed a slew of exciting announcements about HBO’s take on the DC hero. Here’s everything we learned.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The Lanterns panel at San Diego Comic-Con revealed a slew of exciting announcements about HBO’s take on the DC hero. Here’s everything we learned.

The cast of HBO's Lanterns sat down for an in-depth chat about what viewers can expect from the show, and if there's one thing they made clear, it's that nearly all of them are huge fans of the DC comic. They're extremely dedicated to doing right by the fans, and if there's anything this panel has shown us, it's that they'll have a lot to love when it finally airs in August.

Warning — spoilers for Lanterns below!

1. Sinestro is in the show.

However, it doesn’t seem like he’s the big baddie behind the series' main conflict… at least, not yet. From what we saw, he’s been holed up in a space prison for some time — though he’s somehow still able to know about Hal Jordan’s movements, as well as the fact that he’s taking on an apprentice (or, as he forces Hal to admit, a replacement).

2. Manhunters are the central villains of the series.

In one clip, exclusively shown at San Diego Comic-Con, we saw Hal interrogate an alien masquerading as a former football player, quizzing him on various trivia about pros and famous games. However, when it came to other topics — Harry Potter and Barack Obama, specifically — the manhunter came up blank, leading to a hilarious back-and-forth between the two characters. What’s more, the manhunter claimed to have a nuke-level explosive embedded in his skeleton, saying he was sent to Earth on a top-secret mission. We’ll leave the end of the scene a secret to avoid too many spoilers, but it proves these beings are no small threat to the planet.

3. Nathan Fillion crashed the San Diego Comic-Con panel.

Yep, that’s right — Guy Gardner himself (sans that horrible haircut) showed up midway through the panel to introduce a short clip from the show featuring his character. Thus far, we’re not sure what his role in the series will be, but it seems he’s bringing his signature irreverent flair from Superman into this newest story. (Fillion even wore a shirt that said 'Best Gardner Ever,' clearly leaning into his role as a loveable knucklehead.)

4. Laura Linney is playing a role in HBO’s Lanterns show.

This was one of the last big reveals from the panel. Co-creator Chris Mundy broke the news, saying she will be playing a Guardian, one of the beings in charge of the Green Lantern Corps. He was loath to share any more information, but promised her performance was nothing short of fantastic.

“Yes, Laura's in the show,” Chris said. “Yes, she plays one of the Guardians, who has a lot to say to John about the role of being the Green Lantern. We were very lucky in a lot of ways… I'm not saying anything else, or else this panel will be mad at me.”

Aaron Pierre also chimed in, saying, “She’s like an auntie. She’s a phenomenal artist and creative, and we were massively blessed to have her grace us with her presence and her talent.”

5. The Red Lanterns might make an appearance in the show.

At the tail end of the panel, one final clip was shown, where Hal and John duke it out over who will wear the ring. In the middle of their knock-down, drag-out brawl, a bright red light starts to shine through Hal’s room as a siren blares in the background. The clip cut off right after this, so it’s unclear if the Red Lanterns were behind the light, or if it was the manhunters. Given the color, we couldn’t help but speculate.

These are just a few of the most interesting tidbits revealed during the Lanterns SDCC panel, including an anecdote from Aaron Pierre explaining that he tore his bicep right before his final call to audition for the role of John Stewart.

HBO's Lanterns streams on August 16, 2026.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: San Diego Comic-Con 2026: Everything Announced So Far | Comic Con 2026
items.description: San Diego Comic-Con 2026 has arrived, and we'll be covering all the big news coming out of this weekend, including from our own live show that will be filled with exclusive reveals, interviews, and much more from your favorite shows, movies, comics, games, anime, and collectibles.
items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
San Diego Comic-Con 2026 has arrived, and we here at IGN will not only be covering all the big news coming out of this weekend, but we are also hosting our own live show that will be filled with exclusive reveals, interviews, and much more from your favorite shows, movies, comics, games, anime, and collectibles.

To ensure you don't miss a thing, we'll be rounding up all the biggest moments right here for you, including Marvel Studios' big return to Hall H ahead of Avengers: Doomsday!

Be sure to keep checking back as we'll be updating this roundup as the weekend goes on, and you can also head over to our SDCC watch guide and most anticipated movies and TV shows article to know what to expect!

God of War Laufey SDCC Panel Reveals Release Date, a New Kratos Game, and More

God of War Laufey made a big splash at SDCC during its very own panel, as Santa Monica Studio revealed the game's release date of February 16, 2027, and that a new Kratos-led God of War game is coming after God of War Laufey that will connect to the stories.

5 Biggest Reveals From the Lanterns San Diego Comic Con Panel

Lanterns showrunner Chris Mundy and the cast of Lanterns — Kyle Chandler, Aaron Pierre, Garret Dillahunt, and Poorna Jagannathan — joined us at SDCC, and you can check out the five biggest reveals right here (spoilers ahead)!

The crew also tested their mettle in a quiz called Green Lantern of Metal Band, and Pierre tells us that he had a grisly bicep injury that nearly cost him his Lanterns role. Oh, and we now think we know who the real villain of Lanterns is after watching the newest trailer!

Lanterns: Damon Lindelof Explains the One Rule James Gunn Had for the HBO Series

We had the chance to talk to Lanterns co-creators Damon Lindelof and Tom King about James Gunn's rules for adapting comic book super heroes into movies and television, why Guy Gardner is the main Green Lantern, and what happens when a grizzled Lantern vet like Hal Jordan doesn't want to give up his ring to a younger and more capable Jon Stewart.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Trailer Revealed

Not only did Prime Video reveal a brand-new trailer for Season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power, but it was also revealed that Simon Pegg will be joining the cast as the voice of the Balrog. Yes, you read that right!

The Future's Bright in Blade Runner 2099's Debut Trailer

Alongside revealing the long-awaited trailer for Blade Runner 2099, Prime Video confirmed the series will debut on November 25, 2026.

Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender Stars Confirm the Gaang's Relationship Statuses

The voices behind Aang, Katara, Sokka, Toph sit down with us to talk about the new Avatar animated movie, Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender. The cast talks about the importance of being a good person (and being ripped). They discuss how the gaang has aged and who they have become in their mid-20s.

Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender Creators Talk Seven Havens and 2D Animation

Will we EVER get a live action version of The Promise? What about new shows to fill in the gaps? We talked to the creators of Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender, Bryan Konietzko, Michael DiMartino, and Lauren Montgomery at San Diego Comic-Con about animation styles for future Avatar movies/shows, the announcement of Avatar: Seven Havens, and the brand-new trailer.

Avatar: Seven Havens Gets Paramount+ Release Date and Teaser Trailer

Alongside a premiere date of October 9, Paramount revealed a teaser trailer for Avatar: Seven Havens. This new 26-episode 2D-animated series from Avatar creators Michael DiMartino and Bryan Konietzo revolves around a young Earthbender who discovers she’s the new Avatar after Korra in a world shattered by a devastating cataclysm. In this dangerous era, that title marks her as humanity's destroyer, not its savior. Hunted by both human and spirit enemies, she and her long-lost twin must uncover their mysterious origins and save the Seven Havens before civilization’s last strongholds collapse.

Everything Announced at the Marvel's Wolverine: Deep Cuts SDCC Panel

Learn more about Marvel's Wolverine from our coverage of its SDCC panel, which debuted a new trailer, discussed its various characters, and announced a surprise crossover with Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls.

Spaceballs: The New One Creators on Making Mel Brooks' Yogurt CGI and Paying Tribute to John Candy

Rick Moranis appeared at SDCC alongside Josh Gad to reveal new details for Spaceballs: The New One, including Mel Brooks' now CGI Yogurt and fresh Star Wars gags.

Resident Evil Director Ranks His Favorite Resident Evil Games

Resident Evil director Zach Cregger and the film's star, Austin Abrams, chatted about this much-anticipated movie based on the beloved horror video game franchise, its monster design, and what Cregger's top five Resident Evil games are.

Clayface: Everything We Learned at the DCU Horror Movie's Panel

Clayface is bringing horror to the DCU in a big, goopy way. IGN's Tom Jorgensen catches up with Eric Goldman to break down everything director James Watkins and star Tom Rhys Harries had to say about the upcoming movie.

Clayface's F****d Up Practical Horror Proves Anything Is Possible in the DCU

Matt Hagen is ready for his close up... but trust us, you're not gonna want to get too close. Clayface himself Tom Rhys Harries and director James Watkins joined IGN at SDCC 2026 to discuss the movie's heavy use of practical effects, how Batman: The Animated Series' "Feat of Clay" inspired the film, and whether James Gunn had any specific notes on how Gotham City should be represented in its first live-action DCU appearance.

Brad Bird Debuts New Footage From Ray Gunn and Talks About the Movie's Sci-Fi Noir Approach

At San Diego Comic-Con, director Brad Bird (The Incredibles, Ratatouille) revealed more about his newest animated film, Ray Gunn, and debuted the opening seven minutes of the upcoming Netflix release.

Bird also talked about his long-planned 1906 San Francisco earthquake project that now may become a miniseries.

Seth Green’s Star Wars: Detours Will Finally See the Light of Day

Seth Green’s long-shelved animated Star Wars sitcom Star Wars: Detours will finally find itself in front of the public, albeit as an exhibit at George Lucas’ soon-to-open Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles, California.

Street Fighter: How David Dastmalchian Found His M. Bison

Actor and writer David Dastmalchian is playing M. Bison in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, and he stopped by IGN's balcony at SDCC to talk about developing the character for the new film, his YouTube series where he interviews celebrities in literal coffins, his recently released comics, and a lot more.

Eli Roth Picks the Creepiest Horror Movie Kids of All Time

Director Eli Roth is working on a new horror film called Ice Cream Man and it features a bunch of creepy kids, so we did the obvious thing: We asked him what his Mount Rushmore of scary movie kids would be!

Can Adventure Time: Side Quest's Jake and Finn Beat Joker With Farts?

Sasha Knight, John DiMaggio, and Niki Yang from Adventure Time: Side Quests came by to talk all about their new show, how Sash prepared to play Finn the Human, and how Jake and Finn would defeat some of comic's biggest and baddest villains, and yes, some of the tactics included farts.

Johnny Depp Meets Fans as Ebenezer Scrooge, as First Trailer Drops for His Big Hollywood Return

Johnny Depp is making his big Hollywood return in Ebenezer Scrooge, and he celebrated the moment by coming to SDCC as his character. Oh, and they also released the film's trailer!

Superman vs Homelander vs. Kratos: Superman Ranks the Superdads

Jack Quaid and Alice Lee came to our live show to talk all about My Adventures With Superman, how they've grown into their characters, and why Superman would be such a better dad that other popular dads like Kratos, Darth Vader, and Homer Simpson.

X-Men '97 Season 3 Will Bring Back These Fan-Favorite Mutant Villains

During SDCC's 'Marel Comics to Screen' panel, new details about X-Men '97's third and fourth seasons were revealed, including the return of several mutant villains.

Marvel Comics Makes Eddie Brock Venom Again

Fans of Eddie Brock as Venom, rejoice! Marvel revealed that Eddie will become Venom again in a new ongoing series launching after the Queen in the Black crossover wraps up.

President Curtis Tackles the Deficit and Vampires in this Rick & Morty Spin-Off

Keith David, Stephanie Beatriz, Jim Rash, Dan Harmon, and James Siciliano all stopped by our live show to tell us about their new show, President Curtis. Come learn why this character was the best to spin off from Rick & Morty, how Keith David prepares to play the president full time, and much more.

Amazon Prime Has an Exclusive Batman Video Game Set to Launch Alongside Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2

Amazon and Warner Bros. have announced Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles, a new Batman game exclusive to Amazon Prime set to launch on July 31 alongside Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2.

Garfield: Escape from Monday — Official 8-Minute Gameplay Video

We were able to present eight minutes of gameplay from Garfield: Escape from Monday, and you can check out how our favorite lasagna-loving, Monday-hating cat steps into a food-filled world, collects cheese, and jumps around in this upcoming 3D platformer that is set to be released on September 24, 2026.

Nimrods Is Green Day’s First Movie… Will American Idiot Be Their Next?

Legendary punk rockers Billie Joe Armstrong, Tré Cool, and Mike Dirnt take the IGN stage with Mason Thames and director Lee Kirk to explain why Nimrods, a movie loosely based on Green Day's early touring days, takes the road trip comedy approach. Plus, now that Green Day's had a taste of seeing their music fueling a movie, we find out whether or not we're any closer to seeing one of their signature albums, American Idiot, adapted for the big screen.

Marvel Is Finally Publishing New Indiana Jones Comics

While it isn't a new movie, it was revealed at SDCC that we will be getting new Indiana Jones stories thats to Marvel Comics in December 2026.

Dan Houser on Physical Games: "If People Want That, I Think Companies Should Provide It"

After working on games like Grand Theft Auto 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, Dan Houser and Lazlow are keeping their partnership alive through Absurd Ventures. The pair stopped by our live show to share updates on their current projects, including . We also asked them about the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the death of physical media, and more.

American Caper From Absurd Ventures' Dan Houser Is Getting a Double-Sized Season Finale Issue #12

IGN can exclusively reveal that American Caper, the crime fiction comic series from the mind of Absurd Ventures' Dan Houser, is getting a double-sized season finale issue #12 that will arrive on November 11, 2026.

What's Inside This Gaming Handheld and Laptop? Legion 7A and Legion Go 2

We stopped by the Restart Gaming Lounge, where players competed in Marvel Rivals and Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game, to check out the laptops and handheld gaming devices that were powering the competition.

What Else to Expect From IGN's Live Show at SDCC

Day 1:

  • Lanterns
  • Blade Runner 2099
  • Adventure Time: Side Quests
  • The Vampire Lestat
  • Carrie
  • Regular Show
  • My Adventures with Superman

Day 2:

  • The Walking Dead
  • The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power
  • Control Resonant
  • Star Trek: Strange New Worlds
  • Dungeon Crawler Carl
  • Mayday

items.title: Paramount and Warner Bros. Deal Officially Paused, Could Be on Hold Until June 2027
items.description: Paramount has agreed to postpone its Warner Bros. merger until after the conclusion of an antitrust trial, which could keep the deal from closing until June 2027.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Paramount has agreed to postpone its Warner Bros. merger until after the conclusion of an antitrust trial, which could keep the deal from closing until June 2027.

Paramount agreed to refrain from closing the deal as the antitrust lawsuit recently launched by a coalition of 12 states progresses (via Variety). The update confirms the company won't make its grasp on Warner Bros. official until five days after the case's conclusion or June 2027.

"Today’s agreement is a significant win because the result is exactly what we have sought from the outset: a direct path to a trial based on the evidence," a Paramount spokesperson said in a statement. "This is the fastest and clearest way to prove that this transaction is good for competition, good for consumers, and good for creators, a conclusion dozens of competition authorities around the world have already reached.

"'Plaintiffs' market definitions bear no relationship to the realities of today's marketplace and cannot withstand scrutiny. We look forward to proving our case at trial."

Paramount launched a hostile bid for Warner Bros. just days after Netflix announced it had acquired the HBO company in December of last year. The events that followed eventually saw Netflix exit the acquisition altogether, leaving only Paramount to claim victory.

It's been far from an easy road, however, with many entities emerging to challenge the deal. The 12-state coalition, led by California, launched its suit July 13 in hopes of "fighting for a free and fair market and a thriving film and television industry that serves creatives and audiences alike." Earlier this week, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin ordered a two-week pause for the merger that would see the deal barred from being completed until August. Now, with no trial date set yet, it could be on hold for nearly a year.

"Our argument against this illegal merger is straightforward: When too few corporations have too much power in markets central to American life, it makes things more expensive, and it makes things worse," California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a statement. "Today's agreement is great news for audiences, movie theaters, and the many people who write, build, and create the art, news, and entertainment so many of us enjoy. We are eager to continue to make our case in court and celebrate another tremendous win in our effort to ensure this unlawful merger never sees the light of day."

What started as the latest in a series of smaller roadblocks for Paramount has morphed into what could be a nearly year-long delay for the $110 billion Hollywood deal. As noted by Variety, a delay of this length is quite the blow to Paramount, which had been hoping to close its Warner Bros. merger much earlier. Starting September 30, 2026, the company will begin accumulating a fee of $7 million per day, which will be paid to Warner Bros. investors.

For now, it's unclear when the Paramount-Warner Bros. deal will close. With at least a few months to go as the antitrust lawsuit gets off the ground, Paramount's fight to take over the company is just beginning.

Photo by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images.

items.title: Aaron Pierre Reveals Grisly Bicep Injury That Nearly Cost Him Lanterns Role
items.description: Aaron Pierre explained that he nearly didn’t get his role as John Stewart in HBO’s Lanterns series due to a gnarly bicep injury he sustained mere months before filming.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Aaron Pierre explained that he nearly didn’t get his role as John Stewart in HBO’s Lanterns series due to a gnarly bicep injury he sustained mere months before filming.

Pierre shared the shocking story at the official Lanterns panel at San Diego Comic Con, saying he went to his final callback while his arm was still in a brace while he was recovering from surgery.

“Just before we started filming, my tendon separated from the bone,” he said, drawing sympathetic gasps from the audience. “My bicep went all the way up to my shoulder. This was right at the point where I was gonna finally meet Chris and Damon and Tom. I remember my team gave me a call and said, ‘Look, you have this opportunity. You are in the final two or three.’

“I just had surgery and I'm walking around like this,” he continued, mimicking his arm in a sling. “I can't fully extend my arm. They said, ‘You still wanna do it?’ I said, ‘Don't ask silly questions.’ I went into the callback in my brace."

Throughout the panel, Pierre made his love for the Lanterns extremely clear, even wearing a custom letterman jacket emblazoned with ‘In brightest day, in blackest night’ on the back (as well as some special Green Lantern-themed kicks). For him, playing John Stewart was so important that he would do anything — even show up to his final callback in a brace to prove his dedication to the part.

“I just wanted the role so much,” he said. “I love John so much. I think in that moment — this isn't hyperbole — I was like, ‘What would John do?’ I walked in there and gave it my best. I got the role, and I had a matter of months to rehab. I had a fantastic team.”

Pierre isn't alone is suffering a grisly bicep tear; Ryan Hurst, formerly cast as Kratos in Prime Video's God of War series, was forced to leave the project after tearing his bicep filming a stunt for the show. The role will now be recast, with filming projected to resume in 2027.

HBO’s Lanterns streams on August 16, 2026.

items.title: Brad Bird Debuts New Footage From Ray Gunn and Talks About the Movie's Sci-Fi Noir Approach | Comic Con 2026
items.description: At San Diego Comic-Con, director Brad Bird (The Incredibles, Ratatouille) revealed more about his newest animated film, Ray Gunn, along with debuting the opening seven minutes of the upcoming Netflix release.
items.author: Eric Goldman
items.content:
At San Diego Comic-Con, director Brad Bird (The Incredibles, Ratatouille) revealed more about his newest animated film, Ray Gunn, and debuting the opening seven minutes of the upcoming Netflix release.

Bird was the subject of a spotlight My Cinematic Journey SDCC panel in Hall H, hosted by Collider EIC Steven Weintraub. Bird recounted how his elevator pitch for the film was "Buck Rogers meets The Maltese Falcon," describing it as a film about "desperate characters in an alternate future."

The opening scenes give us a look at the film's setting, a futuristic city filled with giant, brilliantly lit towers and flying cars, but with an art deco/1930s vibe to it. It's like if Coruscant was mashed together with Batman: The Animated Series' Gotham City. We see flying cars with art deco design elements, and businessmen in suit and ties taking off into the air on jet packs, while holding old school briefcases by the handle. Jetpacks are omnipresent, including on construction workers, who use them to float about the building they're working on.

"It's Buck Rogers meets The Maltese Falcon."

Brad Bird previews his new movie #RayGunn at #SDCC. pic.twitter.com/i5nAiqGwBe

— Rotten Tomatoes 🍅 (@RottenTomatoes) July 24, 2026

The brunt of the footage focused on the lanky, one-eyed green alien known as Eyera (voiced by Tom Waits) paying someone off to get a janitor's uniform to sneak into an office where it's revealed his trash can actually contains the title character, Ray Gunn himself (Sam Rockwell). There are shadows aplenty in the noir-infused visuals of the square-jawed, sardonic hero Ray and his pal Eyera searching for secret files, only for a competing duo of aliens showing up to find them as well... and for all four to be interrupted by the large, hulking female alien whose office they're breaking into.

It turns out this lady and Ray know each other, as her four extra arms are revealed during a furious fight that culminates in Ray saving himself by using a freeze ray device in her office to form solid ice around her head. But when Eyera tries to get them to run out of there before the cops arrive, Ray proves he's got a good heart by not letting her suffocate, insisting they stay to smash open the ice first. It takes a bunch of very funny Looney Tunes-style bashes of her head back and forth to crack it open properly.

As he had when he spoke to IGN recently, Bird reiterated the very long journey to get Ray Gunn made, noting it had taken 30 years. "I would have happily made it a long time ago, but you need someone to pay for it," Bird quipped. "I always liked it and always thought it would be a good movie."

Bird stressed the importance of fully building out the film's setting, Metropia, noting the movie takes place nearly entirely in this city, which he described as "sci-fi but very urban." Bird and his animators worked to pack the frames with details. "You can let your eye drift and there will be something for it," he said.

Ray Gunn is scored by Michael Giacchino, who has scored all of Bird's movies since The Incredibles. Giachinno made a surprise appearance at the panel, noting he mixed many elements into the music, saying it included "'50s sci-fi, '30s and '40s noir, some slight jazz.”

He said that his big concern was that the score didn't sound like The Incredibles, but stressed that he loves working with Bird because the director likes to switch things up "and takes a hard left turn with his stuff."

Added Giachinno, "At its core, [Ray Gunn has] a very emotional score but it has a lot of action, a lot of fun, and hopefully is its own thing."

Ray Gunn debuts on Netflix on December 18, 2026.

For more on Brad Bird at SDCC, see what he had to say about turning another movie he's developed for decades — a live-action project `about the 1906 San Francisco earthquake — into a miniseries instead.

items.title: Chuck Russell, Director Behind A Nightmare on Elm Street 3 and The Mask, Dead at 74
items.description: Chuck Russell, the director behind movies like The Mask and A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors, has died at 74.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Chuck Russell, the director behind movies like The Mask and A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors, has died at 74.

The filmmaker behind some of the most memorable movies of the '80s, '90s, and 2000s unexpectedly passed away at his San Diego-area home Wednesday, July 22, 2026, his family told TMZ. Details regarding his death were not immediately made clear, though the site said that the local fire department was dispatched to his home Wednesday afternoon "following a report of a medical emergency involving an unconscious male."

Russell, born in May 1958, made his directing debut with 1987's A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors. It brought an impactful start to his career as a director and was immediately followed by his The Blob remake in 1988.

Russell then went on to team with Jim Carrey to deliver quintessential '90s film The Mask in 1994. In 1996 and 2000, he released Eraser and Bless the Child, respectively, and in 2002, helped bring Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson to the big screen with The Scorpion King.

Russell's career as a director then slowed down in the 2000s, with his next project, Fringe, arriving six years later in 2010, and I Am Wrath then premiering in 2016. The final three films he directed were Junglee (2019), Paradise City (2022), and Witchboard (2024).

Russell's The Mask earned an Oscar nomination at the 67th Academy Awards in 1995. Fans of his work have already taken to social media to share their condolences with his family and fond memories of his work.

Chuck Russell, the director behind movies like The Mask and A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors, has died at 74.

The filmmaker behind some of the most memorable movies of the '80s, '90s, and 2000s unexpectedly passed away at his San Diego-area home Wednesday, July 22, 2026, his family told TMZ. Details regarding his death were not immediately made clear, though the site said that the local fire department was dispatched to his home Wednesday afternoon "following a report of a medical emergency involving an unconscious male."

Russell, born in May 1958, made his directing debut with 1987's A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors. It brought an impactful start to his career as a director and was immediately followed by his The Blob remake in 1988.

Russell then went on to team with Jim Carrey to deliver quintessential '90s film The Mask in 1994. In 1996 and 2000, he released Eraser and Bless the Child, respectively, and in 2002, helped bring Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson to the big screen with The Scorpion King.

Russell's career as a director then slowed down in the 2000s, with his next project, Fringe, arriving six years later in 2010, and I Am Wrath then premiering in 2016. The final three films he directed were Junglee (2019), Paradise City (2022), and Witchboard (2024).

Russell's The Mask earned an Oscar nomination at the 67th Academy Awards in 1995. Fans of his work have already taken to social media to share their condolences with his family and fond memories of his work.

items.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved Secret Ending Cutscene Suggests a Halo 2 Remake Is on the Way
items.description: Halo Studios seems to have teased a Halo 2 remake in a secret ending cutscene for Halo: Campaign Evolved.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Halo Studios seems to have teased a Halo 2 remake in a secret ending cutscene for Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Microsoft's Halo 1 remake is finally out in the wild for those who gained early access by purchasing its Premium or Collector's Editions. Just one day removed from its early launch, that means many have already blown through the game multiple times, and some have even discovered a tease for a Halo 2 remake.

Those who manage to beat Halo: Campaign Evolved on Legendary difficulty will be greeted with a new secret cutscene featuring none other than Sergeant Johnson (via ComicBook). Beginning by showing him watching a clip from the original secret ending, Johnson ditches the Elite to kick up his feat on the beach. Just after catching an explosion on the ring, he makes his exit, but not before dropping that tease: "See you in the sequel."

As if that wasn't already enough, another post-credits tease offers even more evidence to suggest a Halo 2 remake is in the cards. In the scene, players can see 343 Guilty Spark flying toward a planet, likely to meet up with Arbiter and launch into the events of the original sequel game. YouTube channel GamersPrey uploaded the full ending sequence here.

It wouldn't be a surprise to see Halo Studios and Xbox continue with a follow-up – or maybe even two – now that a re-imagining for the original is here. However, the pair have yet to announce a proper Halo 2 remake, so the future of the series in general mostly remains a mystery, for now.

Last week, YouTuber Rebs Gaming and Windows Central reported that the developer had most recently canceled a Halo multiplayer game. The project was said to be being worked on by Certain Affinity under the codename "Ekur." That leaves Halo: Campaign Evolved as the only game to carry single-player fans of the franchise until more is shared in the future.

Halo 2 launched for the original Xbox in 2004 and received the remaster treatment with the Master Chief Collection in 2014. Halo: Campaign Evolved, meanwhile, will deliver its remake of the first game when it launches July 28, 2026. Until then, and until Halo Studios is willing to share more about its potential future remake plans, you can check out IGN's 7/10 review of the new game.

"Halo: Campaign Evolved speaks to the series' timelessness and adds a decent set of new missions," we said, "but it's mostly a lean retread that's more of a test run for its future with Unreal Engine."

items.title: Incredibles Director Brad Bird's Long-Planned 1906 San Francisco Earthquake Project Could Become a Miniseries | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Brad Bird reveals at San Diego Comic-Con why his long-gestating 1906 San Francisco earthquake movie is now being planned as an eight-episode miniseries.
items.author: Eric Goldman
items.content:
At San Diego Comic-Con Thursday, The Incredibles and Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol director Brad Bird revealed he's looking to turn his long-in-development project about the 1906 San Francisco earthquake into a miniseries.

This project goes way back for Bird, with the first reports that he was considering making it as a feature film dating back to 2007. It was meant to be his live-action debut, but never came to be, with Bird instead making Ghost Protocol.

Bird dismissed what he referred to as "BS stories online" at the time that the movie version was halted because of budget concerns. Instead, he said, it simply was a situation of not being able to figure out how to fit everything he wanted to into one film.

As Bird explained, when he began to research the 1906 quake, "the deeper I dug, the more stuff [I'd find]." At a certain point, he felt like he was cutting too much, which is why a miniseries would be a natural fit. Though he cautioned it would indeed need a large budget because "it has to be big like a movie.”

Bird's comments about the project were made during the Brad Bird: My Cinematic Journey panel at SDCC, hosted by Collider EIC Steven Weintraub. When Weintraub asked how Bird envisions the miniseries, he remarked, "It’s probably like eight episodes. But it has the greatest build ever. It’s not just the earthquake, it’s the fire after earthquake."

He went on to note that the fire that followed the earthquake was fed by giant winds that "got to be like gale force."

Understandably, much of the panel was focused on Bird's next project, the animated movie Ray Gunn releasing on Netflix this fall. Incredibles 3 was also mentioned, with longtime Bird collaborator, composer Michael Giachinno (who also scored Spider-Man: Brand New Day), making a surprise appearance. Bird reiterated that he is not directing Incredibles 3 — Pete Sohn (Elemental) will direct — but he is co-writing (alongside Dana Murray) and producing the project.

As for Giachinno's involvement, when the composer coyly asked who's doing the score, Bird joked, "the ghost of Jerry Goldsmith” before deadpanning: “We’ll talk about it." That's probably a confirmation Giachinno will indeed return for the next installment of the Incredibles franchise.

Bird also mentioned a bit about another project he has in development — one that could potentially happen before the 1906 miniseries. Bird didn't want to reveal many details, but said it was a film he'd direct. “It’s live-action, but there’s animation in it.”

items.title: In The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3, the Balrog Speaks — and It's Simon Pegg | Comic Con 2026
items.description: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 features a creature famous for failing to pass Gandalf in The Fellowship of the Ring — and, for the first time ever, it speaks.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 features a creature famous for failing to pass Gandalf in The Fellowship of the Ring — and, for the first time ever, it speaks.

At San Diego Comic-Con 2026 today, Prime Video debuted a trailer for Season 3 and revealed three new characters: Eddie Marsan (Happy-Go-Lucky) plays King Durin IV’s older brother, Thrain; Andrew Richardson (Guys & Dolls) plays Elendil’s younger son and Isildur’s brother, Anarion; and Adam Young (Don’t Breathe 2) plays Marnûkh, who is described as “a mysterious Orc who may not be what he seems.” They join the previously announced Jamie Campbell Bower as Celeborn, and Zubin Varla as Khamûl the Easterling.

But the headline addition here is Simon Pegg of Shaun of the Dead and Hot Fuzz fame as the voice of The Balrog — yes, The Balrog, Tolkien’s terrifying creature born of fire, darkness, and shadow who battles Gandalf on the bridge of Khazad-dûm. At SDCC, Prime Video debuted an in-room only featurette titled Bringing Season 3’s Creatures to Life, which showed highlights of several creatures that will be seen this season, including Fell-beasts, the war elephants known as Mûmakil, Orcs, and the return of the Balrog, who for the first time ever will speak.

The Balrog does not speak at any point in any of Tolkien’s texts, nor is there an indication in any of his texts that Balrogs generally are able to speak. So The Rings of Power really is doing something quite different here.

You might remember that in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 2, the Balrog was awakened prematurely from its slumber beneath the Misty Mountains by the greedy Dwarves' mining for mithril. King Durin III sacrifices himself in Khazad-dûm to stop the ancient monster after removing his corrupting ring.

In Season 3, Sauron learns the power to forge the One Ring from the Balrog itself. During the SDCC panel featurette, the showrunners described the Balrog as an "intelligent dangerous adversary," adding: "We want to show a different side of him. We are crazy stupid or wild enough to think in this season he should have a scene with Sauron." Is this the same Balrog we saw in Season 2, or a different one? It's unclear at this stage.

The new teaser shows off the “darker tone” Season 3 is going for, as it depicts Sauron’s quest to forge the One Ring. As we know, Jamie Campbell Bower (Stranger Things) plays Galadriel’s long-lost husband, Celeborn, and Zubin Varla (Andor) plays Khamûl the Easterling, of Rhûn, who goes on to become the second-in-command of the Nazgûl and the only Ringwraith besides the Witch-king named explicitly in J.R.R. Tolkien's core writings.

Season 3 features the Nazgnagôl, the earlier Second Age incarnation of the Nazgûl we know from the Third Age. This means we’ll get to see the origins of the Ringwraiths, who were men working for Sauron and lusting for power. It’s worth remembering that The Rings of Power is set thousands of years before the events of J.R.R. Tolkien’s The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings books, so much of what we see in the show is forgotten by the time Gandalf knocks on Bilbo Baggins’ door.

The first four episodes of Season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power will premiere on November 11, 2026. Episodes five and six will be available to stream on November 18, and the final two episodes of the season will be released on November 25.

Now is the mighty hour. Watch the Official Teaser Trailer to The Lord of The Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3, streaming November 11 on Prime Video. pic.twitter.com/3cktqVK8cH

— The Lord of the Rings (@TheRingsofPower) July 24, 2026

Here’s the official blurb:

In Season 3, Middle-earth is at war. Five years have passed since the fall of Eregion. Sauron’s armies have marched across the whole of the world, conquering all in their path. Only a few isolated pockets stand between the Dark Lord and total victory — Khazad-dûm, where the Dwarves are now sealed deep within their mountain halls, and the elven realms of Lindon and Rivendell, which are protected by their Three Rings. But deep in the land of Mordor, in his newly completed tower of Barad-dûr, the Dark Lord toils day and night, obsessed with harnessing a power that will bring the last of his enemies to their knees: One Ring to rule them all... Now, all the free peoples of Middle-earth — Dwarves, Elves, Men, and Wizards alike — must find a way to come together, in a race against time to prevent Sauron from achieving his goal of utter domination of all life…

Amazon says The Rings of Power is one of the highest performing and most-viewed titles ever on Prime Video. Season 1 is the biggest TV series premiere in the history of Prime Video, and Season 2 is among the Top 5 most-watched returning seasons ever. The series has attracted over 185 million viewers worldwide. The Rings of Power is still on-track to run for five seasons, with the $1 billion show reportedly still under the protection of Amazon boss Jeff Bezos' "magical halo" despite its huge costs.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Marvel Is Finally Publishing New Indiana Jones Comics | Comic Con 2026
items.description: At long last, Marvel Comics is kicking off a new line of Indiana Jones comics, starting with Indiana Jones and the Sword of Pandemonium in December.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
It's been well over a decade since Disney acquired Lucasfilm Ltd. And while they wasted no time in taking advantage of the Star Wars franchise on the publishing side, they've been strangely reticent to focus on Indiana Jones. Even when Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny hit theaters in 2023, there was no new Indiana Jones comic to be had. But there's finally some good news on that front, as Marvel has revealed a new Indiana Jones comic launching in December 2026.

The news broke during the Lucasfilm Publishing panel at SDCC 2026. The new series in question is called Indiana Jones and the Sword of Pandemonium. This five-issue limited series is a direct follow-up to the original Raiders of the Lost Ark movie.

Indiana Jones and the Sword of Pandemonium is written by Jason Aaron, who previously helmed Marvel's 2015 Star Wars series. The book is illustrated by Aaron Kuder (Daredevil), and the first issue features cover art by Kuder, Bryan Hitch, and Alex Ross.

Here's the official description for Indiana Jones and the Sword of Pandemonium #1:

In the wake of Indiana Jones and the Raiders of the Lost Ark, Indy’s most notorious villains, including the impossible return of an archenemy, seek a terrifying new source of power to recoup their loss—one that’s fallen into the hands of his former companion, Marion Ravenwood. Now, Indiana Jones has to race to the far corners of the globe in search of a biblical weapon, embarking on an epic quest that will put both his archeology skills and skepticism of the supernatural to the ultimate test!

This new series looks to be the first step in Marvel's larger plans for the Indy franchise, with the solicitation teasing that the book is "Kicking off a new era of Marvel Comics Indiana Jones Storytelling."

What new Indy adventures do you want to see from Marvel? Let us know in the comments.

Check out IGN's SDCC hub page for more coverage from the convention, including a first look at Hasbro's Legend of Zelda figures and early details on the new Maximum X-Men comic.
